pure-announcement.rationale: It describes a development methodology with worked examples and measurement criteria, not a product launch or release note — the accompanying blog series is incidental.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts cover skills format, MCP platform patterns and OSV; none covers spec-first stories or wave-based parallel agent execution.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The methodology's artifacts are all in the public repo and its central claim is testable through the metrics it itself prescribes, such as merge-conflict and first-pass acceptance rates.

durability.rationale: The process patterns — spec-first stories with acceptance criteria and file boundaries, wave-based parallel execution, review gates, and coordination metrics — are tool-agnostic mechanisms that will hold up regardless of which coding agents are in fashion in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: A team can act on it directly: decompose an epic into stories with explicit file ownership, run independent stories as parallel waves, and measure merge conflicts, first-pass acceptance and escaped defects to improve the decomposition.

atomicity.rationale: The core idea — coordination breakdown, not model capability, is why agents fail, so treat the specification as the program within a wave-based process — states in one paragraph; the adapter directory layout and MCP config sections are repo packaging, not competing ideas.
